lines.text: Thirty-five thousand euros. Gone in a single click.
Monday, seven a.m. Claire, executive assistant at Arkos Systems.
Coffee. Metro. Inbox.
Nine thirty-one: the CEO emails her. Urgent transfer, thirty-five thousand euros. And not a word to anyone.
No time to check. Claire approves.
The next day, the real CEO calls: “What transfer?”
Thirty-five thousand euros lost. In France, this scam cost five hundred and sixteen million euros in 2025.
What if Claire had Solen?
Solen knows every supplier: their IBAN, their phone number, their usual amounts.
These profiles come from payment history, never from an email. Nuvio Cloud: twenty-two payments to the same IBAN since 2019.
On every email, the code checks the sender, the bank details and the amount.
Then the AI reads the request, without ever seeing the IBAN, and exposes the trap: a fake pretext, a deadline that's too short.
The AI can make the verdict stricter. Never softer.
Nuvio announces new bank details? Alert as soon as it's opened.
The IBAN doesn't match the profile.
Solen has you call back the known number, never the one in the email.
Claire's fake CEO? Blocked. A CEO doesn't email from Gmail.
Authority, secrecy, bypassing the hierarchy: everything is explained.
A genuine urgent email gets through, with no false alarm.
Twenty-eight cases replayed: twenty-six out of twenty-six attacks blocked. Zero false alarms.
Even a lookalike address is caught.
Solen. Stopping email scams at the source.
